I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. Wheat and maize — that is what I grow, that is what my father grew. I know this rotation. I know this soil. At 78, I am not going to experiment.

My land is about 4 mu. My youngest son helps me during planting and harvest when the work is heavy, but I handle the day-to-day myself. My knees are bad, so I cannot do as many irrigation trips to the pump as I used to. I will be careful about that.

**Wheat** goes in first, after the maize comes off in September. I will do rotary tillage — the rental machine comes through the village, I pay my share. I will use the Jimai variety seeds I bought last year, the improved ones the township has been pushing. Not the expensive hybrid seeds — wheat doesn't need that and I cannot justify the cost. I put in fertilizer before sowing, mostly urea and diammonium phosphate mixed together like I always have. I will water three times: once before sowing to wet the bed, once in winter to protect the roots from freezing, once at jointing. I used to do four waterings but I will skip the heading irrigation this year — it is a long walk to the pump and the well is getting deeper.

**Maize** goes straight in after wheat harvest in June. No tillage — I just punch the seeds into the stubble rows. My son helps with this. I buy hybrid seed from the county supply co-op, Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever they have. Maize feeds itself more than wheat. Two irrigations — one at planting if it is dry, one at silking. One spray for pests if I see them.

I keep my yields modest. I am not pushing the land.
